candidate_method_families: zero-density or zero-count control of the incomplete-Li remainder
tool_applicability_notes: T-XM-ROOT-BRIDGE-STABILITY-AUDIT applies because the proposed surrogate is aggregate zero counting/density or a finite prime truncation, while the root-useful conclusion is a uniform all-n finite-place/incomplete-Li bound. DifferenceWitness: the target bridge is a power-sum/radial-outlier implication, not a continuum limit. The cheapest check is to preserve the count premise while planting one symmetry-compatible radial outlier and ask whether the power-sum bound survives.

T-RH-LI-PREFIX-QUARTET-CALIBRATION is reused only as an exact regression against finite-index reasoning. DifferenceWitness: RH-ANA-003 does not claim a finite prefix proves RH; it asks whether a purported uniform tail/density theorem genuinely rules out the same delayed off-line mechanism. Exact quartet algebra is a hostile logic test, not zeta evidence.
failure_reuse_notes: F-RH-ANA-001-FINITE-LI-PREFIX rules out treating any finite prime/zero/Li computation as the missing all-index theorem unless a new uniform bridge is separately proved.

F-RH-ANA-002-SUZUKI-NORM-NO-WEAKER-BRIDGE warns against relabeling a root-equivalent condition as a positive surrogate. Any proposed weighted radial bound must be audited for whether it already excludes every off-critical zero and is therefore RH-equivalent.

Neither failure blacklists explicit-formula, density, mollifier, resonance, or growth methods. They constrain the authority of finite surrogates and require a DifferenceWitness when those methods are reused.
unresolved_warnings: Lagarias' strongest incomplete-Li error control in the cited section has RH-sensitive inputs; do not cite it as an unconditional proof bridge.
A density theorem that allows even one fixed off-line zero can remain compatible with the usual zero-counting law while failing a power-sum bound.
A direct prime-side estimate may exploit cancellation unavailable in a zero-density abstraction; route-pruning density alone must not be overgeneralized to all explicit-formula methods.
Palojarvi gives zero-free-region/Li detection results, not an RH proof; constants and hypotheses must remain source-bound.
Any new inequality proposed after this review must be frozen as a candidate and counterexample-tested before theorem search.
